bolus calcium treatment of hypocalcemia is effective in raising calcium concentrations but that the duration of the response is relatively short and that the response is not linear.
calcium gluconate is the treatment of choice for hypocalcemia, but it should be given in small aliquots over a period of 30 minutes.
bolus calcium infusion in the neonatal intensive care unit setting may be a reasonable and safe method of treatment in the acute setting of hypocalcemia in the neonate.

the short-term biochemical effects of bolus calcium treatment of early onset neonatal hypocalcaemia can be described in terms of the peak increase and the rate of decrease in the serum calcium and ionised calcium concentrations.

the rapid decrease in serum calcium concentrations following calcium infusion in neonates is not due to renal loss but rather is due to skeletal retention.
